title: Open Science Society: A Scalable and Decentralized Framework for Fraud-Resistant Peer Review
content: Traditional scientific publishing and bibliometric models face severe limitations regarding prolonged operational processing times, institutional costs, and vulnerability to systemic evaluation biases. To address these inefficiencies, this paper introduces the Open Science Society (OSS), a scalable, decentralized methodology designed for trusted, fraud-resistant scientific curation and real-time peer-evaluation. Moving away from static, global metric indices and opaque review architectures, the proposed framework implements an endogenous, dynamic evaluation method that calibrates reviewer authority scores based on specialized expertise. Crucially, the methodology computes continuous evaluation weights by projecting domain-specific interaction histories onto a keyword-driven semantic space via a symmetric correlation matrix. Through rigorous mathematical formalization and empirical simulation, we demonstrate that the OSS pipeline effectively isolates strategic manipulation, collapsing the voting weight of unqualified actors or collusive networks to absolute zero while preserving genuine cross-domain authority. The system achieves fast, stationary score convergence, establishing a sustainable algorithmic blueprint to ensure long-term publishing integrity and decentralized bibliometric governance without centralized gatekeepers.
